lessons.goal: 理解單位定義並換算食譜中的容量。

questions.evidence: While making soup with his father, Evan reads an old recipe that asks for three cups of water. He reaches for a large drinking cup and begins to fill it. His father points to a note at the bottom: in this recipe, one cup means two hundred milliliters.
questions.prompt: What does one recipe cup mean?

questions.evidence: The drinking cup holds two hundred and fifty milliliters when full. Three of those would add more water than the recipe specifies. They find a measuring jug with clear milliliter marks and decide to use the stated volume rather than count ordinary cups.
questions.explanation: 改用有毫升刻度的量壺。
questions.prompt: Which tool do they use for the stated volume?

questions.evidence: Evan pours six hundred milliliters into the pot. He then checks the other ingredients, because the word cup might otherwise lead him to repeat the same mistake. The recipe's measurements depend on its defined unit, not on whichever container happens to be nearest.
questions.explanation: 同樣單位誤認可能影響其他配料。
options: All ingredients must use six hundred milliliters.
They may use the same easily misunderstood cup unit.
Water is the only ingredient in every soup.
The father has removed all numbers.
questions.prompt: Why check the other ingredients too?

questions.explanation: 食譜先明定cup代表多少容量。

questions.evidence:
While making soup with his father, Evan reads an old recipe that asks for three cups of water. He reaches for a large drinking cup and begins to fill it. His father points to a note at the bottom: in this recipe, one cup means two hundred milliliters.

The drinking cup holds two hundred and fifty milliliters when full. Three of those would add more water than the recipe specifies. They find a measuring jug with clear milliliter marks and decide to use the stated volume rather than count ordinary cups.

Evan pours six hundred milliliters into the pot. He then checks the other ingredients, because the word cup might otherwise lead him to repeat the same mistake. The recipe's measurements depend on its defined unit, not on whichever container happens to be nearest.

After lunch, he rewrites the water line as six hundred milliliters, followed by three recipe cups in brackets. The extra explanation will help another family member follow the old instructions without needing to remember the size of a particular drinking cup.
